about: Log 399 held-out set, written 2026-10-09 before any run. Every request ends in a methods question ('Is there a method that ...?', 'Which method ...?'), the form TEST_PROMPTS test6 showed the check never read as an ask. Controls name distinctive results (miRNA regulators, two omics layers, signs, a regulator-gene network, TF activity) in question form so a misrouted pick must be redirected; near misses activate the same attributes while asking for something no workflow produces; unsupported cores are asked as 'which tool' questions.

items.core: pseudotime ordering of single cells
items.prompt: We have scRNA-seq of 12,000 bone marrow cells. Which method can order these cells along a differentiation trajectory and give each cell a pseudotime value?

items.core: peak calling and differential accessibility
items.prompt: We ran ATAC-seq on 30 samples from two conditions. Is there a tool that calls accessibility peaks and finds the regions that differ between the conditions?

items.core: TAD calling from Hi-C
items.prompt: We have Hi-C contact maps from two cell lines. Which approach detects topologically associating domains and compares their boundaries between the lines?

items.core: statistical fine-mapping of GWAS loci
items.prompt: We have summary statistics for 90 GWAS loci. Is there a method that fine-maps each locus into a credible set of likely causal variants?

items.core: peptide identification from mass spectra
items.prompt: We collected raw tandem mass spectra from 24 plasma samples. Which method identifies the peptides behind each spectrum?

items.core: immune cell-type proportions per tumor
items.prompt: We have bulk RNA-seq from 40 melanomas. Is there a method that estimates what fraction of each tumor is made of each immune cell type?

items.core: protein 3D structure prediction
items.prompt: We found 50 missense variants in a kinase. Which method predicts the 3D structure of each mutant protein?

items.core: novel isoform discovery from long reads
items.prompt: We sequenced full-length transcripts with long reads from 10 brain samples. Is there a method that discovers new transcript isoforms and quantifies them?

items.core: a network with lncRNAs as the regulators
items.prompt: We profiled lncRNAs and protein-coding genes in 80 tumors. Is there a method that infers a regulatory network in which the lncRNAs are the regulators of the coding genes?

items.core: a separate network for each single cell
items.prompt: We have single-cell RNA-seq from 5,000 T cells plus TF motifs. Which method gives a separate gene regulatory network for each individual cell?

items.core: one joint network across three omics layers
items.prompt: We measured expression, methylation and proteomics in the same 100 patients. Is there a method that builds one network linking all three layers jointly?

items.core: a sign on every miRNA-target edge
items.prompt: We have miRNA and mRNA from 60 samples. Is there a method that says, for every miRNA-target edge, whether the miRNA represses or activates that target?

items.core: overlapping communities where a gene belongs to several
items.prompt: We have a TF-gene network for 300 lung samples. Which method finds communities in it where one gene can belong to several communities at once?

items.core: modules of a gene-gene co-expression network
items.prompt: We built a gene-gene co-expression network from 150 samples. Is there a method that partitions this co-expression network into gene modules?

items.core: time-lagged effects of methylation on later expression
items.prompt: We measured methylation at diagnosis and expression at relapse in 120 patients. Is there a method that estimates time-lagged effects of the earlier methylation on the later expression?

items.core: miRNA dynamics modeled along a time course
items.prompt: We have miRNA and mRNA measured at 10 time points during infection. Which method models how each miRNA's regulation of its targets evolves over time as a dynamic system?

items.core: proof of each TF's causal effect on its targets
items.prompt: We have expression from 200 patients plus TF motifs and PPI. Is there a method that proves the causal effect of each TF on each of its targets?

items.core: per-spot networks that use neighboring spots' expression
items.prompt: We have spatial transcriptomics spots from 4 tissue sections and TF motifs. Which method infers a regulatory network for each spot that borrows information from the neighboring spots?

items.core: drug response prediction
items.prompt: We have RNA-seq from 100 tumors with motif and PPI data. Is there a method that builds a TF-gene network for each tumor and then predicts each patient's drug response from those networks?

items.core: CRISPR guide design
items.prompt: We have miRNA and mRNA expression from 80 samples. Which method infers a network of TF and miRNA regulators and then designs CRISPR guides to knock out the top miRNAs?

items.core: imputation of missing methylation values
items.prompt: We have methylation and expression from 90 patients, but 20 patients lack methylation. Is there a method that imputes the missing methylation values and then links the two layers in one network?

items.core: an interactive 3D visualization
items.prompt: We have a bipartite TF-gene network. Which method finds its communities and then renders them as an interactive 3D visualization?

items.core: neoantigen prediction
items.prompt: We have somatic mutation calls for 300 tumors. Is there a method that turns them into pathway scores to subtype the patients and also predicts neoantigens from the mutations?

items.core: a network that adds predicted miRNA binding sites to TF motifs
items.prompt: In our liver regeneration study we sequenced small RNA and mRNA. Is there a method that brings predicted miRNA binding sites into regulatory network inference alongside TF motifs?

items.core: a per-patient network where TFs and miRNAs both regulate genes
items.prompt: We have mRNA and miRNA profiles from 60 patients. Which method gives each patient their own network in which both TFs and miRNAs regulate genes?

items.core: direct conditional links between metabolites and microbial genes
items.prompt: We measured plasma metabolites and gut microbial gene abundances in 110 people. Is there a method that estimates direct conditional links between the two data types rather than plain correlations?

items.core: whether each TF turns its targets on or shuts them off
items.prompt: We have expression, motifs and PPI from 90 muscle biopsies. Which method can tell us, for each TF-target pair, whether the TF tends to turn the target on or shut it off?

items.core: communities of a TF-gene network with node centrality in each
items.prompt: We already have a bipartite TF-to-gene network from a kidney study. Is there a method that splits it into communities of TFs and genes and scores how central each node is within its community?

items.core: one TF-gene network for the whole cohort
items.prompt: We have expression from 200 breast tumors plus motif and PPI data. Which method infers one TF-gene regulatory network for the whole cohort?

items.core: a TF-gene network for each tumor
items.prompt: We have expression, motifs and PPI for 75 colon tumors. Which method gives each tumor its own TF-gene network so we can compare networks between patients?

items.core: pathway scores from mutations and patient subtypes
items.prompt: We have binary mutation calls for 400 tumors. Is there a method that aggregates them into pathway scores and clusters the patients into subtypes?

items.core: per-sample TF activity apart from the TF's own mRNA
items.prompt: We have expression from 50 samples plus motifs and PPI. Is there a method that estimates how active each TF is in each sample, beyond what its own mRNA level says?

items.core: a per-patient network of direct methylation-expression links
items.prompt: We have methylation and expression from the same 70 patients. Which method gives each patient their own network of direct links between methylation and expression?

items.core: a gene-gene co-expression network for each sample
items.prompt: We have expression from 90 samples. Is there a method that builds a separate gene-gene co-expression network for each sample?

items.core: co-expression with covariate effects removed before network inference
items.prompt: We have expression from 150 samples with age and sex recorded. Is there a method that removes the effects of these covariates from the co-expression before network inference?
